previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and prior Puestow procedure was admitted for elective repair of a symptomatic incisional hernia that had caused a minor bowel obstruction. He underwent an uncomplicated open ventral incisional hernia repair with Prolene mesh overlay on hospital day one. Postoperatively, he was managed with IV fluids, antibiotics, a JP drain, and pain control via PCA initially, transitioning to oral medications. His diet was advanced from clear liquids on postoperative day one to a regular diet by day three. He voided independently after catheter removal, remained afebrile, and had stable vital signs. He was discharged home on postoperative day three with instructions for incision and drain care, oral Keflex, and follow-up. His chronic conditions, including hypertension, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and diabetes, were managed with continuation of most home medications.
problems: Incisional hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

likely explanation for patient's GI symptoms.  CT torso 
performed on admission revealed no etiology for abdominal pain.  
Pt was evaluated by surgery given his recent ventral hernia 
repair and wound appeared clean/dry/intact.  Surgery consult

admitted for pain control and rehydration.  Pt was treated

out PE which revealed a 1.7 cm R hilar LN.  The patient had no

nightsweats.  PCP was notified regarding these findings as was

.
# Sinus Tachycardia:  On admission, patient's HR was in 110s 
likely related to pain and volume depletion.   Tachycardia 
improved to baseline HR of 90-100s with IVF and pain control.    

.

syncope/presyncope related to acute episodes of abdominal 
discomfort.  The history sounded most consistent with 
vasovagal/hypovolemic syncope given the setting, chronicity and 
absence of ever sustaining injury. An Echo was performed this 
admission that showed no evidence of outflow tract obstruction 
and preserved EF.  He was monitored on telemetry and cleared by 
___ prior to discharge.

chest pain several days PTA that was exertional, associated with 
nausea and L arm numbness and lasted approx 30 mins.  He did not 
have any chest  pain in house and echo did not reveal any wall 
motion abnormality.  Given his risk factors, he was instructed

radiology_notes.text:
CLINICAL HISTORY: Dyspnea.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  The lungs are
clear bilaterally demonstrating no focal consolidation, effusion or
pneumothorax.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  Osseous structures are
intact.  No free air below the right hemidiaphragm is seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intrathoracic process.

CLINICAL HISTORY: Abdominal pain status post ventral hernia surgery on
___.  Evaluate for obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Upright and supine radiographs of the abdomen were obtained.  The
bowel gas pattern is unremarkable without evidence of ileus or obstruction. 
Surgical clips are noted in the right upper quadrant, likely from prior
cholecystectomy.  A tube projects over the abdomen of unknown etiology.  There
is no evidence of free air.  Bony structures appear intact.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of bowel obstruction or free air.

INDICATION:  ___ man with shortness of breath and syncope and belly
pain.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were acquired with contrast through the chest, abdomen
and pelvis.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:

The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There is no axillary or mediastinal
lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria. An enlarged right hilar lymph node
measures up to 1.7 cm in short axis. There is no evidence of pulmonary
embolism or acute aortic syndrome. There is a tiny pericardial effusion.  The
visible lungs show mild bibasilar atelectasis.  No nodules, masses, or
effusions are present.  The airways are patent down to the subsegmental level.


CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:

The liver, spleen, both adrenals, both kidneys are normal.  The patient is
status post cholecystectomy and a ventral hernia repair with drain placed in
the superficial skin overlying the anterior abdomen.  There are calcifications
within the pancreas consistent with chronic pancreatitis.  Post-surgical
changes from prior Puestow procedure with Roux-en-Y pancreaticojejunostomy and
distal enteroenteric anastomosis are again seen. Prominent loop of bowel at
the enteroenteric anastomosis is again seen without evidence of high grade
obstruction. No pelvic or abdominal free fluid or free air is present.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:

The rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, prostate, and seminal vesicles are normal.
No pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria or pelvic free fluid
is present.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

The visible osseous structures show no fractures, suspicious lytic or blastic
lesions.

IMPRESSION:

1. No evidence of pulmonary embolism or acute aortic syndrome.

2. Non-specific enlarged right hilar lymph node; differential includes
inflammatory, infectious, neoplastic etiologies.  Recommend clinical
correlation and follow-up.

3. No acute CT findings in the abdomen or pelvis.

Findings/recommendation under #2 above were submitted to radiology critical
findings dashboard on ___.
